big_idea: Mindfulness, paying attention on purpose, in the present moment, without judgment, is available to anyone in ordinary daily life, not just seated meditators. Kabat-Zinn frames it as a way of being rather than a technique for achieving anything.

tool.label: The seven attitudinal foundations
tool.text: Kabat-Zinn organizes the practice around seven attitudes to cultivate together: non-judging, patience, beginner's mind, trust, non-striving, acceptance, and letting go.
tool.note: These same seven attitudes first appeared in his clinical book Full Catastrophe Living and are restated here as short, personal essays rather than a formal checklist.

ideas.title: Present-moment awareness
ideas.text: Most people live filtered through memories, plans, and mental commentary, missing the actual experience happening right now.

ideas.title: Non-doing
ideas.text: Mindfulness isn't about achieving a state or fixing yourself; it's about stopping the constant doing mode and simply being aware.

ideas.title: The breath as anchor
ideas.text: The breath is a steady point of attention to return to whenever the mind wanders, in formal practice or daily life.

ideas.title: Autopilot awareness
ideas.text: Habitual, automatic behavior, like walking, eating, or listening, can be interrupted by deliberately noticing bodily sensations and surroundings.

ideas.title: Patience as practice
ideas.text: Losing your patience compounds a loss: don't let circumstances take your mind after they've already taken your time.

ideas.title: No single right method
ideas.text: Meditation has no fixed formula; consistency and honest attention matter more than duration or technique.

try_it: Pick one routine activity this week, like climbing stairs or washing dishes, and do it once a day with full attention instead of autopilot.
Sit for 2 to 5 minutes each morning, following your breath and gently noting when your mind wanders, without judging the wandering.
During one unavoidable wait this week, practice staying present instead of mentally fighting the wait.
Pick one of the seven attitudes, like beginner's mind, and notice a moment each day you could approach as if for the first time.
best_for: Meditation beginners wanting an approachable entry point
Anyone wanting to build reflection into ordinary daily moments rather than a formal practice
less_useful: Readers wanting structured step-by-step MBSR instruction, which is more Full Catastrophe Living's territory
Readers who prefer secular, clinical framing over reflective, essay-style prose
